processing: Little is documented for this garden. Darjeeling black tea is normally withered, rolled, oxidised and fired in the orthodox way, more lightly in spring.
harvest_season: As usual in Darjeeling, first flush in spring and second flush in early summer, then monsoon and autumn pickings.
appearance_dry: Typical of Darjeeling, mixed olive and brown twisted leaf with some pale tips, darker in later flushes.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold to amber, depending on the flush.
appearance_wet: Soft green-and-copper leaf in spring, browner later in the year.
taste_profile: No tasting record specific to this garden is well established. As with other Darjeelings, expect floral briskness in spring and rounder fruit in summer.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Use about 85°C for a spring lot.

vintage_note: Usual for Darjeeling: sold by year and flush, with a lot number and leaf grade when sold as a single estate. Spring lots are best within about a year. Rangaroon rarely appears under its own name, so a dated lot is worth checking closely.
description:
Rangaroon is a small-profile Darjeeling garden, known mostly as a name on the roster of Darjeeling Organic Tea Estates, the group that also runs Ambootia, Happy Valley and Monteviot.

Few details of its leaf or processing are in print, so anything said about the cup is really about Darjeeling in general: orthodox processing, light oxidation in spring, fuller in summer.

Brew it like other Darjeelings, cooler and shorter for first flush. If you come across a dated lot, compare it with a sister garden from the same group and season.

Do not confuse it with Rangdoo, the original name of Okayti, which is a different estate.
history:
Little is documented about Rangaroon's past. A travel listing places it about 27 km from Darjeeling on the Peshok road and gives 1840 as its founding year, a very early date that has no firmer backing and should be read with caution.

It is listed today among the gardens of Darjeeling Organic Tea Estates Private Ltd.
